scope: 30 unprocessed GSC examples (9 NL, 21 EN): 21 new synopses and nine adequate stored synopses preserved; one additional reading-link destination repaired.
method: Live audit of 50 remaining canonical sitemap pages. Prioritize all 13 without a source-backed synopsis in initial HTML; include four URLs with exact (low-volume) impressions in the saved performance export, then 13 pages with useful opportunities for series/format clarification and contextual reading links. Not a popularity ranking and no claim that these issues caused Google exclusion. Existing verified synopsis text can be retained when adequate.
notes: Indexing is not guaranteed. Selection is not a popularity ranking.
All 25 selected Open Library editions passed exact ISBN, language and parent-Work checks; five native catalog editions retain their previously verified identities.
Publisher sources may describe another edition of the same work; ISBN and language remain unchanged.
No stored descriptions overwritten; existing stored-first resolution preserved.
Human + Machine: exact 2018 ISBN and coauthor verified in publisher-supplied Google Books metadata.
The author website for Tempestuous Reunion contains a conflicting blurb; the matching Harlequin synopsis was used instead.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"To restore family honor the Marquess of Rotherstone faces his most dangerous mission--finding the perfect bride. To London's aristocracy, the Inferno Club is a scandalous society of men no proper young lady would acknowledge.
But though they are publicly notorious for pursuing all manner of debauchery, in private they are warriors who would do anything to protect king and country. The Marquess of Rotherstone has decided it's time to restore the family's good name.
But as a member of the Inferno Club, he knows there is only one way to redeem himself in Society's eyes: marry a lady of impeccable beauty and breeding, whose reputation is, above all, spotless. Someone quite unlike Daphne Starling. True, she's temptingly lovely, but a jilted suitor has nearly ruined her reputation.
Still, Max cannot resist her allure--or the challenge of proving London's gossips wrong. He would do anything to win her hand-- and show that even a wicked marquess can make a perfect husband" -- from publisher's web site.
pages.title: My Wicked Marquess
pages.author: Gaelen Foley
pages.text:
Max, the Marquess of Rotherstone, needs a respectable marriage to repair his family's reputation. His interest in Daphne Starling complicates that plan: she has already paid a social price for refusing an unwanted suitor. Behind Max's scandalous public image lies his involvement in the secretive Inferno Club.

The first Inferno Club novel combines Regency courtship with the dangers of a hidden mission. Daphne must judge the man behind the rumours, while Max's obligations make trust difficult. The romance develops through questions of reputation, independence and the secrets a prospective partner chooses to keep.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Once upon a time, in small-town India, there lived two intelligent boys. One wanted to use his intelligence to make money. One wanted to use his intelligence to create a revolution. The problem was, they both loved the same girl. Welcome to Revolution 2020.
A story about childhood friends Gopal, Raghav and Aarti who struggle to find success and love in Varanasi. However, it isn't easy to achieve this in an unfair society that rewards the corrupt. As Gopal gives in to the system, and Raghav fights it, who will win?
pages.title: Revolution 2020
pages.author: Chetan Bhagat
pages.text:
Gopal, Raghav and Aarti grow up together in Varanasi, but their ambitions pull them towards different futures. Gopal wants financial security and success; Raghav wants to challenge the corruption around him. Both are in love with Aarti, making their disagreements personal as well as political.

Chetan Bhagat places this love triangle within India's competitive education business, where money and influence can determine who gets ahead. The novel asks what someone is prepared to compromise to escape poverty, and what happens to friendship when private desires collide with public ideals.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Barcelona, 1957. It is the week before Christmas in the Sempere & Sons bookshop. Daniel Sempere is happily married to Bea, and they have a son, whilst their partner Fermin is soon to marry Bernarda. Luck, finally, seems to be smiling on them.
Then a mysterious person enters the shop, buys the most expensive volume on display — an illustrated edition of The Count of Monte Cristo — and inscribes in it the words 'For Fermin Romero de Torres, who came back from among the dead and holds the key to the future. 13'. Who is he? What does he want?
The answer lies in a terrible secret, hidden for two decades. ..a tale of imprisonment, betrayal, murder- and love, leading back into the heart of the Cemetery of Forgotten Books. --back cover
pages.title: The Prisoner of Heaven
pages.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
pages.text:
A stranger arrives at the Sempere bookshop in Barcelona at Christmas in 1957, threatening to expose a secret from Fermín Romero de Torres's past. Daniel Sempere follows his friend into a story of imprisonment, loyalty and revenge rooted in the early years of Franco's dictatorship.

This third Cemetery of Forgotten Books novel reconnects characters and mysteries from The Shadow of the Wind and The Angel's Game. Fermín's history becomes the focus, while the bookshop and the hidden lives surrounding it keep literature at the centre of the investigation. Reading the earlier novels first gives the returning relationships more context.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming how we work right now. Are you ready? In the past, robots were typically large pieces of machinery, sectioned off from human workers to perform precise, mechanical tasks on an assembly line.
But now, bots and other AI technologies go far beyond this in augmenting human capabilities--not just robots on the factory floor of an auto plant, but algorithms in the back office of a healthcare insurer and chatbots interacting with retail customers.
Unlike any software tool or service that's come before, artificial intelligence has the power to profoundly change the very nature of work itself--and this is happening in all kinds of enterprises and across all functions of the organization.
There's a current and growing imperative: businesses that understand how to harness AI can surge ahead, while those who neglect it are in danger of being left behind. In Human + Machine, Accenture technology leaders H. James Wilson and Paul R. Daugherty vividly illustrate how AI is redefining work and the economy.
At the core of this paradigm shift is the transformation of business processes--all the step-by-step tasks that take place within an organization, from operations to customer service to workers' own personal productivity habits.
As humans and smart machines collaborate ever more closely, work processes become more fluid and adaptive, enabling companies to change them on the fly--or completely reimagine them.--
pages.title: Human + machine
pages.author: Paul R. Daugherty
pages.sourceName: Harvard Business Review Press via Google Books — 2018 edition
pages.text:
Paul R. Daugherty and H. James Wilson examine how organisations can redesign work when people and artificial intelligence collaborate. Their argument goes beyond replacing individual tasks: they describe new combinations of human judgement and machine capabilities, and the roles needed to make those combinations useful.

Drawing on research across businesses, the authors discuss changes to workflows, management and employee skills. This is the original 2018 edition, written for readers considering the organisational consequences of AI. It offers a management framework for human–machine cooperation rather than a technical guide to building models.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"Produced with unprecedented access to Cuban national archives, iRevolucion! is the largest collection of these posters ever published.
With an introduction illuminating the rich social and artistic history of the posters, and rare biographical information on the artists themselves, this beautiful volume offers a revealing look at Cuba's efforts to define itself through a potent mix of imagery and politics in striking visual terms."--Jacket.
pages.title: Revolucion!
pages.author: Lincoln Cushing
pages.text:
Lincoln Cushing brings together Cuban posters produced after the 1959 revolution, showing how graphic art carried political messages and promoted cultural life. The collection covers themes including national identity, production, public health, sport, education and international solidarity.

The posters make this a visual history: lettering, colour and simplified images communicate ideas meant to reach a broad public. Context about the designs and their makers helps readers consider both their artistic choices and their political purposes. It is a collection of graphic work and historical commentary, suited to exploring how public images persuade.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"In this book a master scientist tells the great story of how life on earth evolved. Edward O. Wilson eloquently describes how the species of the world became diverse, and why the threat to this diversity today is beyond the scope of anything we have known before."
"The Diversity of Life has quickly become a classic text in its definition of a new environmental ethic - our obligation to rescue ecosystems, not simply individual species - and its prescient call for an end to the conservation versus development argument.
In an extensive new foreword for this edition, Professor Wilson addresses the explosion of the field of conservation biology and takes a clear-eyed look at the work still to be done."--Jacket.
pages.title: The Diversity of Life
pages.author: Edward Osborne Wilson
pages.sourceName: Library of America / Penguin Random House
pages.text:
Edward O. Wilson explores how evolution has produced the variety of life on Earth and how species depend on the ecosystems around them. His account connects the emergence of biological diversity with the processes that can destroy it, moving from the natural history of living organisms to the consequences of human activity.

The book presents biodiversity as more than a count of species: relationships between organisms and habitats are part of what is at stake. Wilson's argument for conservation gives the scientific account a practical urgency. Readers interested in ecology will find a broad explanation of why losing species changes the living systems that remain.

pages.beforeSynopsis: The Jedi Knights lead the battle against a powerful droid army of separatists, while Anakin Skywalker mentors his first Padawan, a girl named Ahsoka, while learning the skills of a warrior and becoming a hero of the Clone Wars, in a novelization of a new television animated feature film and series.
pages.title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
pages.author: Karen Traviss
pages.text:
Anakin Skywalker is given a new apprentice, Ahsoka Tano, while the Republic struggles to hold its position in the Clone Wars. Their mission to recover Jabba the Hutt's kidnapped son carries consequences beyond one rescue: access to Hutt-controlled routes could affect the war. Count Dooku and Asajj Ventress have plans of their own.

Karen Traviss adapts the animated film Star Wars: The Clone Wars into a novel, bringing the campaign, the Jedi and their new partnership onto the page. This is the film's story, with Ahsoka's arrival central to Anakin's changing responsibilities as a teacher.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
The second time around
Once, 27 year old Luc Santini's inherent sensuality had proved to be 18 year old Catherine Parrish's downfall. For two years she had loved him unconditionally, until she realized that this rich, powerful man regarded her as a possession--not a woman he loved enough to marry.
She fled her gilded cage--pregnant with his child. And then, four and a half years later, fate placed Luc back in her life. He didn't know about Daniel... and Catherine intended to keep it that way. But would she surrender to his erotic demands--and risk losing herself in a whirl of desire--to protect her son?
pages.title: Tempestuous Reunion
pages.author: Lynne Graham
pages.text:
Catherine Parrish left Luc Santini while carrying his child, keeping the pregnancy from the wealthy man whose demands had overwhelmed their relationship. When their paths cross again, their unresolved attraction returns alongside the secret she has protected.

Lynne Graham builds this contemporary romance around a reunion complicated by parenthood, mistrust and unequal power. Catherine's decisions about independence and disclosure matter as much as the renewed attraction. Readers can expect an emotionally confrontational second-chance story, in which a shared past makes reconciliation difficult rather than automatic.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Offers writing prompts, activities, and tips and techniques for writing and illustrating a story.
"Have you ever thought about telling your own story, whether it be true or imagined? Are you interested in writing, drawing, or both? If the answers are yes, this fun, colorful, and interactive journal is for you!
With guidance from Raina herself, brainstorm ideas, make lists, paste in personal photos, and use your imagination like never before to create your own stories. For additional inspiration, behind-the-scenes info from Raina's own comics-making adventures is featured inside."--back cover.
pages.title: Share Your Smile
pages.author: Raina Telgemeier
pages.text:
Raina Telgemeier invites readers to turn their own experiences into stories in this interactive journal. Prompts encourage them to recall people, places and moments that matter, then explore those memories through writing and drawing. The creative work belongs to the reader, with Telgemeier's approach to personal storytelling providing a starting point.

Share Your Smile is an activity book for making something, rather than another complete graphic memoir to read from beginning to end. It suits readers who enjoy Telgemeier's comics and want to experiment with telling a story from their own lives.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Whenever foreigners visit Paradise they always ask Darling and her friends to smile for the camera. Here are some of the things Darling and her friends have to smile about: stealing guavas, gifts from NGOs, singing Lady Gaga at the tops of their voices.
But they all want to go to the real paradise in America or Britain.
pages.title: We need new names
pages.author: NoViolet Bulawayo
pages.text:
Darling grows up in Zimbabwe, where games with her friends coexist with hunger, insecurity and the upheavals around them. Moving to America offers a different future, but the distance from home creates losses that cannot be resolved simply by arriving somewhere safer.

NoViolet Bulawayo follows Darling's changing sense of belonging through childhood and migration. Language, memories and the people left behind remain part of her new life. The novel explores the gap between an imagined destination and the complicated experience of living there, with a young narrator attentive to both the absurdities and the pain of the adult world.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
The "French novel about a woman whose mission to cure her "routine-itis" leads her to lasting joy and true fulfillment, for fans of The Alchemist and Hector and the Search for Happiness.
At thirty-eight and a quarter years old, Paris native Camille has everything she needs to be happy, or so it seems: a good job, a loving husband, a wonderful son. Why then does she feel as if happiness has slipped through her fingers? All she wants is to find the path to joy.
When Claude, a French Sean Connery look-alike and routinologist, offers his unique advice to help get her there, she seizes the opportunity with both hands.
Camille's journey is full of surprising escapades, creative capers, and deep meaning, as she sets out to transform her life and realize her dreams one step at a time."--
pages.beforeTitle: Your second life begins when you realize you only have one
pages.title: Your second life begins when you realize you only have one
pages.author: Raphaëlle Giordano
pages.text:
Camille has a job and a family, yet feels that her everyday life has lost its meaning. An encounter with Claude, who calls himself a routinologist, leads her to try practical challenges intended to loosen the habits and assumptions that keep her dissatisfied.

Raphaëlle Giordano uses Camille's story to explore personal change, confidence and attention to daily life. The book blends a fictional journey with ideas drawn from self-development: its exercises and conversations are part of a novel, rather than a clinical treatment programme. It offers an accessible story about reassessing an apparently settled life.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Iedereen met een fobie voor de brievenbus, iedereen die zijn enveloppen dagenlang ongeopend op tafel laat liggen tot hij moedig genoeg is om ze open te maken, zal zich herkennen in Pol Verholst.
Hoewel hij de zoon is van een postbode, en een groot liefhebber van de woorden, is zijn angst voor de post zo groot dat hij willens nillens zijn naam schonk aan een ziekte waar zovelen aan lijden. De angst voor post, oftewel: de Ziekte van Verholst.
Een ziekte die een heel leven kan ruïneren, en waarbij vergeleken de angst voor spinnen of iets als hoogtevrees werkelijk niets meer voorstelt.
pages.title: In weerwil van de woorden
pages.author: Dimitri Verhulst
pages.text:
Pol Verholst is de zoon van een postbode en houdt van woorden, maar ontwikkelt een allesoverheersende angst voor letters. Wat vertrouwd zou moeten zijn, wordt daardoor een bron van gevaar. Zijn pogingen om eraan te ontsnappen maken het dagelijks leven steeds ingewikkelder.

Dimitri Verhulst bouwt deze korte roman rond die onmogelijke verhouding tot taal. De overdreven aandoening geeft ruimte aan satire en vervreemding: juist woorden moeten vertellen wat er gebeurt met iemand die letters niet meer verdraagt. Het boek past bij lezers die houden van een absurd uitgangspunt dat langzaam een heel bestaan ontregelt.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Angel Fire is het tweede deel van de spannende Angel Trilogy. Er is veel gebeurd, engelen zijn niet de goedaardige wezens waarvoor ze zich voordoen, en Willow weet dat. Zelf half-engel, is ze zich ook bewust van de vreselijke plannen van de Engelenkerk.
Alleen zij kan hen tegenhouden, maar dat zal de sekte niet zomaar toelaten, integendeel, de leden van de Engelkerk hebben gezworen dat ze Willow kapot zullen maken. Gelukkig staat Willow er niet alleen voor, er is Alex: vermaard engelendoder, en, Willows enige grote liefde.
Samen willen ze een nieuwe generatie engelendoders opleiden om gewapend te zijn in de strijd. Maar, al doet Alex nog zo zijn best, Willow blijft zich als half- engel een buitenstaander voelen. Wanneer op een dag een bijzonder aantrekkelijke vreemdeling in het kamp toekomt, slaat bij Willow de twijfel toe?
pages.title: Angel Fire
pages.author: Lee Weatherly
pages.text:
Na een nieuwe golf van engelenaanvallen trekken Willow en Alex naar Mexico-Stad. Daar sluiten ze zich aan bij een groep engelendoders die zich voorbereidt op een aanval op de machtige Serafijnse Raad. Willows afkomst als halfengel wekt wantrouwen, terwijl Alex de groep probeert te trainen.

De komst van Seb, die net als Willow halfengel is, maakt hun samenwerking en relatie nog ingewikkelder. Angel Fire is het tweede deel van de Angel-trilogie en gaat verder op de gebeurtenissen uit Angel. De bovennatuurlijke strijd wordt verweven met vragen over loyaliteit, aantrekkingskracht en de behoefte iemand te vinden die je begrijpt.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
An anniversary cruise promises a married couple a chance to enjoy their life together. The holiday ends abruptly when the husband vanishes, leaving his wife to return to the Netherlands without an explanation. Months later, a message from a lender raises questions that her search had not answered.
As she learns about matters he concealed, her attempt to find him becomes an investigation into a marriage she may not have understood.
pages.title: Cruise: A Thriller
pages.author: Suzanne Vermeer
pages.text: An anniversary cruise promises a married couple a chance to enjoy their life together. The holiday ends abruptly when the husband vanishes, leaving his wife to return to the Netherlands without an explanation. Months later, a message from a lender raises questions that her search had not answered. As she learns about matters he concealed, her attempt to find him becomes an investigation into a marriage she may not have understood.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Onnoval wordt op een vollemaannacht ontvoerd door de Griezelbus en belandt tussen de geheimzinnige Reizigers. Terwijl hij verzwakt raakt, dringen herinneringen en dreigende stemmen uit een andere werkelijkheid tot hem door. Liselore vermoedt dat er iets ernstig mis is en zoekt met anderen naar hem.
Dit zevende deel onderzoekt Onnovals verleden en brengt zijn verbondenheid met de bus verder aan het licht.
pages.title: De Griezelbus 7
pages.author: Paul van Loon
pages.text: Onnoval wordt op een vollemaannacht ontvoerd door de Griezelbus en belandt tussen de geheimzinnige Reizigers. Terwijl hij verzwakt raakt, dringen herinneringen en dreigende stemmen uit een andere werkelijkheid tot hem door. Liselore vermoedt dat er iets ernstig mis is en zoekt met anderen naar hem. Dit zevende deel onderzoekt Onnovals verleden en brengt zijn verbondenheid met de bus verder aan het licht.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Rutger Bregman onderzoekt het idee dat mensen van nature vooral op hun eigen belang uit zijn. Met historische voorbeelden en een andere blik op het verleden stelt hij dat gangbare mensbeeld ter discussie. De vraag is niet alleen hoe mensen zich gedragen, maar ook welke gevolgen onze verwachtingen van elkaar hebben.
Dit non-fictieboek combineert een betoog over de menselijke geschiedenis met vragen over vertrouwen en de inrichting van de samenleving.
pages.title: De meeste mensen deugen
pages.author: Rutger Bregman
pages.text: Rutger Bregman onderzoekt het idee dat mensen van nature vooral op hun eigen belang uit zijn. Met historische voorbeelden en een andere blik op het verleden stelt hij dat gangbare mensbeeld ter discussie. De vraag is niet alleen hoe mensen zich gedragen, maar ook welke gevolgen onze verwachtingen van elkaar hebben. Dit non-fictieboek combineert een betoog over de menselijke geschiedenis met vragen over vertrouwen en de inrichting van de samenleving.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Dubravka Ugrešić onderzoekt in deze roman hoe verhalen ontstaan en hoe mensen in andermans levensbeschrijvingen terechtkomen. De sluwe, van gedaante wisselende vos uit oosterse overleveringen vormt een terugkerend motief.
Literaire zijfiguren en ogenschijnlijke voetnoten krijgen ruimte naast reizen door verschillende landen en tijden. Fictie, herinnering en biografische bijzonderheden lopen daarbij in elkaar over.
Het boek vraagt wie een verhaal mag bepalen en wat er gebeurt met de mensen die in een bekendere geschiedenis meestal buiten beeld blijven.
pages.title: De vos
pages.author: Dubravka Ugrešić
pages.text: Dubravka Ugrešić onderzoekt in deze roman hoe verhalen ontstaan en hoe mensen in andermans levensbeschrijvingen terechtkomen. De sluwe, van gedaante wisselende vos uit oosterse overleveringen vormt een terugkerend motief. Literaire zijfiguren en ogenschijnlijke voetnoten krijgen ruimte naast reizen door verschillende landen en tijden. Fictie, herinnering en biografische bijzonderheden lopen daarbij in elkaar over. Het boek vraagt wie een verhaal mag bepalen en wat er gebeurt met de mensen die in een bekendere geschiedenis meestal buiten beeld blijven.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
In the future, abortion has become a crime as a series of events threatens the existence of the United States. One woman wakes up to discover that her skin color has been changed to red as punishment for having the procedure done.
Now she must embark on a dangerous journey in order to find refuge from a hostile and threatening society.
pages.title: When she woke
pages.author: Hillary Jordan
pages.text:
Hannah Payne wakes to find her skin turned red by the state. In this near-future America, criminal punishment is made visible through genetically altered skin colour, leaving those marked to face public hostility. Hannah must find safety while questioning the religious and political beliefs that once structured her life.

Hillary Jordan's dystopian novel examines shame, bodily autonomy and the consequences of making faith an instrument of government. Its connection to The Scarlet Letter becomes a way to reconsider punishment and social exclusion. The story follows one woman's effort to reclaim her identity in a society determined to define her by a conviction.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Born in the eighth year of Enclosure, ten-year-old Honor lives in a highly regulated colony with her defiant parents, but when they have an illegal second child and are taken away, it is up to Honor and her friend Helix, another "Unpredictable," to uncover a terrible secret about their Island and the Corporation that
runs everything.
pages.beforeTitle: The other side of the island
pages.title: The other side of the island
pages.author: Allegra Goodman
pages.text:
Honor arrives on Island 365 with parents who will not behave as the authorities expect. In a world reshaped by rising seas, the Corporation promises safety through strict rules and controlled surroundings. Honor wants to fit in, but her family's resistance makes their position increasingly dangerous.

When the security she trusts starts to unravel, she must look beyond the explanations she has been taught. Allegra Goodman's novel for younger readers combines a child's wish to belong with a dystopian mystery about obedience and the suppression of difference. The central tension is whether protection is still protection when nobody is free to question it.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Grubbs Grady expects his world to consist of ordinary dislikes, family arguments and tricks played on his sister. A decision not to join a family weekend takes him somewhere far more frightening. Demons and werewolves become immediate dangers rather than things safely contained in stories.
As the familiar boundaries of his life collapse, he has to confront a reality he did not know existed. This novel begins Darren Shan's Demonata series.
pages.title: Demonata #1, The: Lord Loss
pages.author: Darren Shan
pages.text: Grubbs Grady expects his world to consist of ordinary dislikes, family arguments and tricks played on his sister. A decision not to join a family weekend takes him somewhere far more frightening. Demons and werewolves become immediate dangers rather than things safely contained in stories. As the familiar boundaries of his life collapse, he has to confront a reality he did not know existed. This novel begins Darren Shan's Demonata series.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
After a brief encounter at a party, Russ Callaghan and Aurora Roberts unexpectedly meet again as summer-camp counsellors. Both have taken the job partly to get away from difficulties at home. Russ wants distance from his father's gambling problems, while Aurora hopes to recover a sense of belonging.
Working together renews an attraction neither planned to pursue. The camp's rule against relationships between staff makes their summer more complicated than either had intended.
pages.title: Wildfire
pages.author: Hannah Grace
pages.text: After a brief encounter at a party, Russ Callaghan and Aurora Roberts unexpectedly meet again as summer-camp counsellors. Both have taken the job partly to get away from difficulties at home. Russ wants distance from his father's gambling problems, while Aurora hopes to recover a sense of belonging. Working together renews an attraction neither planned to pursue. The camp's rule against relationships between staff makes their summer more complicated than either had intended.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
**Two childhood friends. Two broken hearts. One impromptu road trip to get away from everything. That’s all this was supposed to be. After all, I’ve been living in the friend zone for years now.**
But hockey heartthrob Jasper Gervais isn’t looking at me like a friend anymore. And he isn’t touching me like one either.
To his fans, he’s the handsome, talented athlete on TV. To me, he’s still the lost boy with sad eyes and a heart of gold.
The man I’ve loved in secret for years.
So when my life falls apart on my wedding day, it only makes sense that he’s the one to swoop in and save me. And when his world comes crashing down around him, I’m there to return the favor.
But the more time we spend alone, the more Jasper doesn’t feel like a friend at all. He feels like everything I’ve ever wanted and thought I could never have.
Our feelings aren’t straightforward though. They twist and turn around the pain of his past and the reality of my present.
Jasper Gervais acts like he wants me.
But after years of turning me away, he’s going to need to prove it.
pages.title: Powerless
pages.author: Elsie Silver
pages.text:
Sloane has loved her childhood friend Jasper Gervais for years, even while preparing to marry someone else. When her wedding plans collapse, the professional hockey player helps her escape. A road trip brings them into close contact just as both are dealing with crises they cannot ignore.

The third Chestnut Springs novel turns a long friendship into an uncertain romance. Jasper's difficult past and Sloane's present obligations stand between their attraction and a relationship they can trust. Elsie Silver focuses on the risks of finally saying what has remained unspoken, within the connected small-town world of the series.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
My name is Ivy Westfall. I am sixteen years old and a traitor. Three months ago, I was forced to marry the President's son, Bishop Lattimer - as all daughters of the losing side of the war are sold off in marriage to the sons of the winners. But I was different. I had a mission - to kill Bishop.
Instead, I fell in love with him. Now I am an outcast, left to survive the brutal savagery of the lands outside of civilization. Yet even out here, there is hope. There is life beyond the fence. But I can't outrun my past.
For my actions have set off a treasonous chain of events in Westfall that will change of all our fates - especially Bishop's... and this time, it is not enough to just survive.
pages.title: The revolution of Ivy
pages.author: Amy Engel
pages.text:
Ivy Westfall has been forced beyond the fence that once enclosed her world. Survival now depends on unfamiliar people and choices she must make for herself. Her feelings for Bishop remain tangled with the betrayals and divided loyalties that brought her here.

This is the concluding novel of Amy Engel's Ivy duology and follows The Book of Ivy directly. The focus shifts from the rules of an enclosed society to what freedom demands outside it. Read the first book before this continuation: Ivy's relationship with Bishop and the conflict between their families give her decisions their weight.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Mary Jekyll, alone and penniless following her parents' death, is curious about the secrets of her father's mysterious past.
One clue in particular hints that Edward Hyde, her father's former friend and a murderer, may be nearby, and there is a reward for information leading to his capturea reward that would solve all of her immediate financial woes. But her hunt leads her to Hyde's daughter, Diana, a feral child left to be raised by nuns.
With the assistance of Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson, Mary continues her search for the elusive Hyde, and soon befriends more women, all of whom have been created through terrifying experimentation: Beatrice Rappaccini, Catherine Moreau, and Justine Frankenstein.
When their investigations lead them to the discovery of a secret society of immoral and power-crazed scientists, the horrors of their past return. Now it is up to the monsters to finally triumph over the monstrous.
pages.beforeTitle: The strange case of the alchemist's daughter
pages.title: The strange case of the alchemist's daughter
pages.author: Theodora Goss
pages.text:
Mary Jekyll investigates her father's past after her mother's death leaves her short of money. A possible reward for finding Edward Hyde brings her to his daughter Diana, then to other women whose origins are linked to disturbing experiments. Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson help with an investigation that also involves a series of murders.

Theodora Goss brings figures from Gothic fiction together in the first Extraordinary Adventures of the Athena Club novel. The women whose lives have been shaped by other people's experiments become investigators of their own histories. Literary references, mystery and their competing voices form the book's playful structure.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"Two Gentlemen of Verona is commonly agreed to be Shakespeare's first comedy, and probably his first play. A comedy built around the confusions of doubling, cross - dressing and identity, it is also a play about the ideal of male friendship an what happens to those friendships when men fall in love.
William Carroll's engaging Introduction focuses on the traditions and sources that stand behind the play and explores Shakespeare's unique and bold treatment of them.
Special attention is given to the strong female figure of Julia - a prototype for some of Shakespeare's later and most loved heroines, Viola (Twelth Night) and Rosalind (As you Like It)."--Publisher's description.
pages.title: The Two Gentlemen of Verona
pages.author: William Shakespeare
pages.text:
Shakespeare tests the loyalty of two friends against the demands of romantic love in this early comedy. Disguise, divided affections and mistaken assumptions complicate their relationships, while Julia's actions challenge the idea that the men alone control how the story unfolds.

This Arden Shakespeare Third Series edition includes William Carroll's introduction, which examines the play's sources and traditions, the treatment of friendship and the importance of Julia. It also addresses the controversial final scene. The edition suits readers who want the play alongside critical context for its comic devices and troubling resolutions.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
A moonlit night. A sleeping village. And an unaccountable murder ... An English bobbie returning from night patrol finds a corpse in evening dress locked in the stocks on the village green. He identifies the body immediately.
Andrew Vereker was not a well-loved man, and narrowing down the suspects is not going to be an easy job. The Vereker family are corrupt and eccentric - and hardly cooperative ...
It's another case for the resourceful Superintendent Hannasyde, who sets off on the trail of a killer so cunning that even his consummate powers of detection are tested to their limits ...
pages.title: Death in the stocks
pages.author: Georgette Heyer
pages.text:
A policeman finds Andrew Vereker's body in the stocks on an English village green. The dead man has left few admirers, and his eccentric family gives Superintendent Hannasyde plenty of possible motives but little straightforward help. Sorting out what the relatives mean becomes as important as listening to what they say.

Georgette Heyer combines a murder puzzle with sharp exchanges between difficult, sometimes amusing suspects. Readers who know her historical romances encounter her detective fiction here: the attraction lies in the investigation, the competing accounts and the personalities that complicate the search for the killer.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Katniss Everdeen komt terecht in het middelpunt van het verzet tegen het Capitool. Haar rol als symbool van de opstand brengt mogelijkheden én zware verantwoordelijkheden met zich mee. President Snow gebruikt de mensen om wie zij geeft om druk op haar uit te oefenen.
Terwijl de strijd groter wordt, moet Katniss bepalen welke offers zij kan aanvaarden en hoeveel zeggenschap zij werkelijk over haar eigen rol heeft.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Waar vecht je nog voor als je alles waar je van houdt verliest?
De dag van de boete voor de vijftigste Hongerspelen breekt aan en paniek houdt de districten van Panem in zijn greep. Dit jaar worden er ter ere van de Kwartskwelling twee keer zoveel tributen de afgrijselijke arena in gestuurd worden.
In District 12 probeert Haymitch Abernathy niet te veel na te denken over de kans dat hij een van hen zal zijn. Hij wil gewoon de boete doorkomen en bij het meisje zijn van wie hij houdt. Maar wanneer zijn naam tijdens de ceremonie wordt geroepen verandert die droom in een nachtmerrie.
Hij wordt onmiddellijk afgevoerd naar het Capitool, samen met drie andere tributen: een jeugdvriendin die als een zus voor hem is, een geobsedeerde bookmaker, en het meest verwaande meisje van de stad.
Zodra de Spelen beginnen, beseft Haymitch dat hij gedoemd is te verliezen. Maar iets in hem wil vechten… En hij wil dat zijn strijd tot ver buiten die dodelijke arena nagalmt.
pages.title: Dageraad boven de boete
pages.author: Suzanne Collins
pages.text:
Haymitch Abernathy hoopt op de dag van de boete vooral dat zijn naam niet wordt genoemd. Voor de vijftigste Hongerspelen geldt een extra wrede regel: er moeten twee keer zoveel tributen naar de arena. Wanneer hij toch wordt gekozen, reist hij met drie andere jongeren uit District 12 naar het Capitool.

Deze voorgeschiedenis speelt zich af vóór Katniss' deelname en laat Haymitch zien als een jongen die zelf probeert te overleven. Suzanne Collins onderzoekt hoe een machtsapparaat geweld tot vermaak maakt en welke ruimte er dan nog overblijft voor verzet. Het boek verdiept de geschiedenis van Panem vanuit een andere generatie.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
De natuurkundige Shevek is opgegroeid op Anarres, waar een samenleving zonder het vertrouwde bezit en gezag van de buurwereld is ingericht. Zijn wetenschappelijke werk brengt hem naar Urras. Daar ontdekt hij andere mogelijkheden, maar ook nieuwe vormen van ongelijkheid en afhankelijkheid.
De ontheemde onderzoekt beide werelden zonder een eenvoudig ideaalbeeld te geven. Wetenschap, persoonlijke vrijheid en de vraag hoe mensen hun samenleving organiseren lopen door elkaar heen.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
Een onzekere getuige vertelt Cormoran Strike over een mogelijke moord uit zijn jeugd, maar verdwijnt voordat de detective door kan vragen. Samen met Robin Ellacott onderzoekt Strike het verhaal, dat hen van Londen naar invloedrijke politieke kringen en een landhuis voert.
Hun bekendheid en onderlinge spanningen bemoeilijken het werk. Het vierde boek over het duo verweeft een onderzoek naar het verleden met problemen in hun eigen samenwerking.

pages.beforeSynopsis:
"A short, accesible critical guide to visual culture-what it means to look and see; how the visual impacts our lives, our era, our understandings of each other, and even how it is changing our brains"--
As if John Berger's Ways of Seeing was re-written for the 21st century, Alexis L. Boylan crafts a guide for navigating the complexities of visual culture in this concise introduction. The visual surrounds us, some of it invited, most of it not.
In this visual environment, everything we see--art, color, the moon, a skyscraper, a stop sign, a political poster, rising sea levels, a photograph of Kim Kardashian West--somehow becomes legible, normalized, accessible.
How does this happen' How do we live and move in our visual environments' This volume offers a guide for navigating the complexities of visual culture, outlining strategies for thinking about what it means to look and see--and what is at stake in doing so.
Visual culture has always been inscribed by the dominant and by domination. This book suggests how we might weaponize the visual for positive, unifying change.
Drawing on both historical and contemporary examples--from Judy Chicago's The Dinner Party and Beyoncé and Jay-Z at the Louvre to the first images of a black hole--Alexis Boylan considers how we engage with and are manipulated by what we see.
She begins with what: what is visual culture, and what questions, ideas, and quandaries animate our approach to the visual? She continues with where: where are we allowed to see it, and where do we stand when we look? Then, who: whose bodies have been present or absent from visual culture, and who is allowed to see it?
And, finally, when: is the visual detached from time? When do we see what we need to see?
pages.title: Visual Culture
pages.author: Alexis L. Boylan
pages.text:
Alexis L. Boylan examines how images shape everyday life and how people learn to interpret what they see. Visual culture includes art, advertising, screens and the ordinary surroundings through which ideas about identity and power circulate. Looking is treated as an activity influenced by history and social position.

This short introduction asks readers to reconsider familiar images and the assumptions they bring to them. It offers concepts for discussing the relationship between viewers and visual objects, making it a useful companion to a focused collection of posters, photographs or other public images.
